summary: workflow.sleep() timer persists on the Temporal server when an asyncio.Task wrapping it is canceled, unlike asyncio.sleep() which properly cancels. The SDK fails to send a CancelTimer command, causing the timer to fire on an already-canceled future.
userImpact: Users cannot properly cancel timers created with workflow.sleep(), leading to orphaned timers and potential exceptions when callbacks fire.
rootCause: SDK does not intercept asyncio task cancellation and propagate it as a CancelTimer command to the Temporal server.
proposedFix: Implement proper cancellation propagation for workflow.sleep() to send CancelTimer commands when wrapping asyncio tasks are canceled.
workaround: Use asyncio.sleep() instead of workflow.sleep() for operations that may be canceled.
keyQuote: The Temporal timer is never canceled on the server. No TimerCanceled event appears in workflow history.
